guide.summary: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 code flow where each customer authorizes one registered app, yielding a user-associated token. The files.metadata.read scope with App Folder content access covers listing metadata only, within the app folder.
guide.recommendation: Dropbox uses OAuth 2.0 code flow where each customer authorizes one registered app, yielding a user-associated token. The files.metadata.read scope with App Folder content access covers listing metadata only, within the app folder.

findings.title: Per-user OAuth 2.0 code flow with one registered app
findings.detail: Each user signs in at dropbox.com and approves the app; the app exchanges the returned code at /oauth2/token for an access token. Apps requesting only User API scopes receive a token tied to the authorizing user. Access tokens are short-lived; token_access_type=offline returns a refresh token for background access. The app is registered once; customers must not register their own apps.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer connects an individual Dropbox account to the web app.

evidence.quote: In this flow: * The user will be redirected to Dropbox to authorize your app to access their Dropbox data.
Apps that request only scopes from the User API will receive a token associated with the user that authorizes the app.
Do *not* instruct your users to register their own Dropbox application to use your app - you just need to register your app once. Your end-users will connect to that

findings.title: files.metadata.read scope for listing folder entries
findings.detail: list_folder and list_folder/continue both require files.metadata.read, which covers reading file and folder metadata (names). It does not grant content download or any write capability. Pagination: while has_more is true, call list_folder/continue with the returned cursor.
findings.appliesWhen: Listing entries and continuing until has_more is false.

evidence.quote: **Required scope:** `files.metadata.read` **Endpoint format:** RPC
list_folder. **Required scope:** `files.metadata.read`
- `has_more` (boolean, required) — If true, then there are more entries available. Pass the cursor to list_folder/continue to retrieve the rest.

findings.title: Register app, choose App Folder access, set redirect URIs
findings.detail: Create the app in the Developer Console, choose the scope in the Permissions tab, obtain the app key and secret, and register exact redirect URIs. Choose App Folder content access so actions are limited to the app's folder under /apps. A generated token can test with the developer's own account only.
findings.appliesWhen: Before the first test of the authorization flow.

evidence.quote: of registering your app, selecting permissions, and obtaining an app key and secret (a.k.a. `client_id` and `client_secret`) and inputting redirect URIs.

steps.title: Register the Dropbox app with App Folder access and files.metadata.read
steps.detail: In the Dropbox Developer Console, create ONE app (customers never register their own). Choose content access 'App Folder'. In the Permissions tab enable only the files.metadata.read scope. In Settings > OAuth 2 > Redirect URIs, register the exact callback URL of the web app. Note the app key (client_id) and app secret (client_secret). Chosen client type: confidential web app using the code flow with client_secret kept server-side (no PKCE, no implicit grant; leave 'Allow public clients' off).
steps.doneWhen: App exists with App Folder access, files.metadata.read enabled, exact redirect URI registered, and client_id/client_secret stored securely server-side.

evidence.quote: Before you can get started, you'll need to register your app with Dropbox by creating a new app in the Developer Console. That page will guide you through the process
* You'll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application. Add them under **Redirect URIs** in the OAuth 2 section
* **App Folder:** Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder *only* (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable

fields: client_id: app key from Developer Console Settings tab
client_secret: app secret from Settings tab, server-side only
redirect_uri: exact URI registered under Redirect URIs

steps.title: Send a test account through Dropbox consent and check the callback
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a browser as a representative test Dropbox account: https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=<CLIENT_ID>&redirect_uri=<REDIRECT_URI>&response_type=code&state=<STATE>. The user signs in at dropbox.com and approves. Dropbox redirects to your registered redirect_uri with code and state in the query string; verify state equals what you sent. This step is performed by a person; it is not executed by this plan.
steps.doneWhen: Callback receives a code query parameter and a state matching the one sent.

evidence.quote: 1. Construct a Dropbox authorization URL, with your application’s `client_id` and `redirect_uri` (if applicable) and specifying the `response_type` of `code`, and present it to the user

`https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code` 2. Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code
of the Settings tab. Dropbox checks that the specified `redirect_uri` parameter in your Authorization URL matches one of the registered values at authorization time.

fields: CLIENT_ID: app key from Developer Console
REDIRECT_URI: exact registered callback URL
STATE: random value you generated for this session

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Server-side, POST the code to the token endpoint using client_id and client_secret as form fields. Expected successful output: JSON with access_token (and expiry; refresh_token only if token_access_type=offline was requested). Boundary check: inspect the returned scope value and confirm it contains files.metadata.read and no write or content scopes. Do not run any write call to test read-only behavior.
steps.doneWhen: Response contains access_token and a scope list limited to files.metadata.read (plus account basics).

evidence.quote: 3. Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s `client_secret` to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

When using refresh tokens, your call to the /oauth2/token endpoint with the `grant_type` of `authorization_code` will return a short-lived access token and a refresh token, which should be securely stored.
When using the code flow, your app must keep the `client_secret` secure. If your app can’t guarantee it’s security, then we recommend the use of PKCE as described below

fields: AUTH_CODE: code query parameter from the callback
grant_type: constant authorization_code
REDIRECT_URI: must match the one used at consent
CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET: from app settings, server-side only

steps.title: List entries of the App Folder (first page)
steps.detail: POST list_folder with an empty path, which is the root of the app folder for an App Folder app, using the user's access token. Expected successful output: JSON with entries (files and direct subfolders), cursor and has_more. Names are in entries[].name. Boundary check: this app must never call content download or write endpoints; verify the token scope shows only files.metadata.read and that outgoing request logs contain only list_folder calls. Also confirm an out-of-folder path such as /Documents is not reachable, since App Folder apps cannot see outside it. If entries contain a deleted-tag item, it is not a current file.
steps.doneWhen: Response returns entries with names; note cursor and has_more for continuation.

evidence.quote: # List Folder POST https://api.dropboxapi.com/2/files/list_folder
**Required scope:** `files.metadata.read` **Endpoint format:** RPC
- `entries` (list of files.Metadata, required) — The files and (direct) subfolders in the folder.

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: access_token from the token exchange response
path: empty string means the app folder root

steps.title: Continue listing with the returned cursor until has_more is false
steps.detail: While has_more in the previous response is true, POST list_folder/continue with the cursor from that prior response. Repeat using each new cursor. Stop when has_more is false; that is the documented end condition. Expected output: more entries with names, plus a new cursor and has_more.
steps.doneWhen: A response returns has_more=false, and all pages' entries[].name values have been collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.
